notes:
**A written call that made money was recorded as a loss.** Sell an option at 100, buy it back at 80, and that twenty-rupee profit was booked as a twenty-rupee loss - so the day-loss cap switched the rule off for winning and the Live screen painted every winner red. Worse, the stop on a written option was placed as a SELL: a stop that adds to the position it exists to close.

**Delta rules now actually run.** "Buy when delta crosses 0.5, exit if it falls back to 0.3" backtested correctly and then, once deployed, never fired once - the live runner was never told what the option's delta was, so every comparison came out false and the screen said "no trades yet".

**A rule that says "exit after three bars" now exits after three bars.** The count of bars held was stuck at zero live, so only the stop, the target or the closing bell could end a trade.

**Every AI-built rule is now proved against your own words.** A second reading of your sentence - one that never sees the code - invents test cases, and the code is run on them. Where the two disagree you are shown the exact case.

**Leverage answers to the stock.** Every equity intraday trade got five times leverage regardless. A scrip that swings five percent a day needs a quarter of its value upfront, not a fifth.

**Pay Later interest for every day it was held.** Over a weekend, Monday charged one day for three.

**An options backtest reported no drawdown for a trade that halved.** Only closed trades touched the curve.

**Simple sentences no longer need the AI.** If the app can read your whole sentence it builds the rule itself - free, instant, no key.
